quotes.text: Microsoft is telling the truth when they say co-pilot will not show a user a file they don't have permission to see. That is the baseline, but that baseline assumes your permissions are correct.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why permission-trimmed AI is only as safe as the permissions underneath.

quotes.text: If a sensitive document is technically open, it is now functionally public within your tenant.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Captures how Copilot collapses the gap between possible and actual access.

quotes.text: In a traditional application, the code is separate from the data. You don't execute the data. But in a large language model, the data is the code.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear explanation of why prompt injection is a structural risk for RAG systems.

quotes.text: Restricted SharePoint search isn't a long-term solution for a broken architecture. It is a bandaid on a structural wound.

quotes.text: Whether the AI wrote 10% or 90% of the content, the person who hits "send" or "publish" owns every word, every fact, and every potential error.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concise accountability principle for an AI usage policy.

takeaways: Copilot respects permissions, so a decade of oversharing in SharePoint and Teams becomes an AI exposure problem that must be remediated before licenses are assigned.
Roll out in risk tiers and enforce boundaries with Microsoft Purview: sensitivity labels, adaptive scopes, label inheritance and interaction-level DLP for prompts and responses.
Prove realized value with A/B tests and capacity metrics, govern citizen-built agents and exceptions explicitly, and build a governance-aware culture with champions.
hook: Turning on Microsoft 365 Copilot for everyone can turn a decade of loose SharePoint permissions into a data exfiltration engine. This episode is for IT leaders and architects who need a practical governance model for Copilot, from prompt injection risks and risk-tiered rollout to Purview, DLP and oversharing cleanup. Learn how to make Copilot secure, auditable and worth its license cost.
